terms.definition: Infrastructure owned and operated by third-party cloud providers, shared across multiple customers
terms.example: AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform providing services to thousands of companies

terms.definition: Dedicated cloud infrastructure used exclusively by a single organization
terms.example: A bank building its own cloud environment in its data center using VMware for security compliance

terms.definition: Combination of public and private cloud connected together, allowing workload portability
terms.example: Hospital keeping patient records in private cloud while running website on AWS public cloud

terms.definition: Infrastructure shared among organizations with similar requirements or regulatory obligations
terms.example: Three universities pooling resources to create a shared research computing cloud

terms.definition: Cloud service providing virtualized computing resources where customer manages OS and applications
terms.example: Amazon EC2 - you get a virtual server but must install and configure everything yourself

terms.definition: Cloud service providing complete development platform where customer only manages code and data
terms.example: AWS Elastic Beanstalk - upload your code and AWS handles all infrastructure automatically

terms.definition: Fully managed application delivered over internet where customer only uses the software
terms.example: Gmail, Salesforce, Zoom - just log in and use, no infrastructure management needed

terms.definition: Physical facility housing servers, storage, networking equipment, power, and cooling systems
terms.example: Large building with rows of server racks, backup generators, and air conditioning

terms.definition: Framework defining security and operational boundaries between cloud provider and customer
terms.example: AWS secures the hardware, you secure your data, passwords, and configurations

terms.definition: Technology allowing multiple virtual machines to run on single physical server through software abstraction
terms.example: One server with 32 CPUs running 10 virtual servers, each with 3 vCPUs

terms.definition: Software layer that creates and manages virtual machines, allocating physical resources
terms.example: VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, AWS Nitro System managing VMs on physical servers

terms.definition: Hypervisor installed directly on physical hardware without underlying OS, used in production
terms.example: VMware ESXi, Xen, KVM running directly on server hardware in AWS data centers

terms.definition: Hypervisor running as application on existing operating system, used for development
terms.example: VirtualBox on your laptop running Windows while your laptop runs macOS

terms.definition: Software-based computer with virtual CPU, memory, storage, and network, isolated from other VMs
terms.example: EC2 instance with 2 vCPUs, 8GB RAM, 100GB disk running Ubuntu Linux

terms.definition: Multiple customers sharing the same physical infrastructure while maintaining security isolation
terms.example: AWS running 1000 different companies' EC2 instances on same physical servers

terms.definition: Automatic addition or removal of computing resources based on demand
terms.example: Website automatically launching 10 more servers during Black Friday, then removing them after

terms.definition: Hybrid cloud strategy using public cloud capacity when private cloud reaches capacity limits
terms.example: E-commerce site running normally on private cloud but bursting to AWS during holiday sales

terms.definition: Moving running VM from one physical host to another without downtime
terms.example: AWS moving your running EC2 instance to different hardware for maintenance while it stays online

terms.definition: Allocating storage on-demand as data grows rather than reserving full capacity upfront
terms.example: Requesting 500GB disk but AWS only using 50GB initially, growing as you add files

terms.definition: Allocating more virtual resources than physical capacity, betting not all are used simultaneously
terms.example: Physical server with 256GB RAM hosting VMs totaling 400GB RAM allocation

terms.definition: Security boundary maintained by hypervisor preventing VMs from interfering with each other
terms.example: If one VM crashes or gets hacked, other VMs on same server remain safe and operational

terms.definition: Non-virtualized server providing direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead
terms.example: AWS i3.metal instance for high-frequency trading requiring absolute minimum latency

terms.definition: Lightweight virtualization sharing OS kernel, faster and smaller than VMs
terms.example: Docker container running your application, starting in seconds vs minutes for VMs

terms.definition: Template containing OS and pre-configured software for launching EC2 instances
terms.example: Pre-built Ubuntu image with Apache and MySQL installed, ready to launch in 60 seconds

terms.definition: Upfront spending to purchase physical assets like servers
terms.example: Buying 100 servers for $500,000 before you can use them

terms.definition: Ongoing pay-as-you-go spending for services consumed
terms.example: Paying AWS $5,000/month for EC2 instances you actually use
